relevance_reason: This is a single case report of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis that was diagnosed by histology, with no genetic testing, plus a review of previously published cases. It adds clinical evidence but no new molecular findings.

findings.statement: Mikilita et al. (2020) reported an 8-year-old Brazilian girl with a diffuse skin disorder that began in the first months of life. She had erythematous, scaly, hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent borders on the mesogastrium, cubital and popliteal fossae, and inguinal and cervical regions. She also had palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on the scalp and nasal introitus, with no changes in hair, nails, or mucosa. There was no family history and no consanguinity. One month later the affected areas had grown larger but were no longer polycyclic, showing that the plaques were migratory.
quotes: An 8-year-old female patient was attended at the pediatric dermatology outpatient clinic of the Hospital Santa Casa of Porto Alegre with a report of diffuse dermatosis that began in the first months of life.

the patient presented erythematous, scaly, hyperkeratotic plaques with prominent borders, affecting the mesogastrium, cubital fossae, popliteal fossae, and inguinal and cervical regions, as well as palmoplantar hyperkeratosis and yellowish hyperkeratotic plaques on the scalp and nasal introitus
After one month, she was reassessed and the appearance of the plaques changed, increasing the extension of the affected areas; however, the polycyclic aspect disappeared

findings.statement: In the patient reported by Mikilita et al. (2020), a skin biopsy from the forearm showed acanthosis, papillomatosis, and hyperkeratosis with marked epidermolysis of the granular layer. The authors had first suspected erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva, but this epidermolytic hyperkeratosis led them to diagnose annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.
quotes: Skin biopsy in the extensor portion of the forearm showed acanthosis, papillomatosis, and hyperkeratosis with marked epidermolysis in the granular layer

The initial hypothesis was erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva; however, the finding of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis in histopathological examination led to the diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.

findings.statement: Mikilita et al. (2020) identified erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (EKVP) as the main differential diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis. They listed onset during childhood, absence of epidermal fragility, and histology without epidermolysis as features that distinguish EKVP.
quotes: The main differential diagnosis of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is with erythrokeratodermia variabilis et progressiva (EKVP)
Distinctive features of EKVP include onset during childhood, absence of epidermal fragility, and histology without evidence of epidermolysis.

findings.statement: Mikilita et al. (2020) reviewed 19 previously reported cases from 10 publications. Topical treatments, including retinoids, corticosteroids, propylene glycol, calcipotriene, and keratolytics, produced little response. Three articles reported a good response to systemic retinoids: two with acitretin and one with low-dose isotretinoin.
quotes: found 19 cases in 10 publications that are summarized in table 1.
Three articles report good response with systemic retinoids; two articles cite acitretin treatment with good response, and another reports good response with low doses of isotretinoin.

relevance_reason: Reports a third kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis and a novel KRT10 helix termination mutation.

findings.statement: Suga et al. (1998) described a third kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, a phenotypic variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma. Affected individuals present with bullous ichthyosis in early childhood and hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in flexural areas and extensor surfaces at later ages, and characteristically develop intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.
quotes: Individuals with this variant present with bullous ichthyosis in early childhood and hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in the flexural areas and extensor surfaces at later ages.
Characteristically, they also develop intermittent bouts of annular and polycyclic, erythematous, scaly plaques on the trunk and proximal extremities.
We now describe a third kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis.

phenotypes.text: hyperkeratotic lichenified plaques in flexural areas and extensor surfaces
intermittent annular and polycyclic erythematous scaly plaques on trunk and proximal extremities

findings.statement: In a kindred with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, Suga et al. (1998) identified a novel mutation in the KRT10 gene resulting in an ile107-to-thr substitution (codon 446) within the highly conserved helix termination motif at the end of the rod domain of keratin 10.
quotes: Molecular analysis of this family revealed a novel mutation resulting in an isoleucine to threonine substitution at residue 107 (codon 446) within the highly conserved helix termination motif at the end of the rod domain of keratin 10.

variants.as_reported: isoleucine to threonine substitution at residue 107 (codon 446)

relevance_reason: Reports a second family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis and identifies the causative KRT10 mutation.

findings.statement: Joh et al. (1997) reported a family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis in which two generations were affected. The proband had bullous ichthyosis with episodes of disease activity, during which many annular and polycyclic erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques appeared on the trunk and proximal extremities. Histology showed the typical pathology of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis. On ultrastructural analysis, keratin filament networks were abnormal and tonofilaments formed clumps around the nucleus.
quotes: Here we report a second incidence of this disorder in a family with two affected generations.

The proband suffered from bullous ichthyosis and had bouts of disease activity associated with the development of numerous annular and polycyclic erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and the proximal extremities.

Histologic examination showed the typical pathology of epidermolytic hyperkeratosis, and ultrastructural analysis revealed abnormal keratin filament networks and tonofilament clumping with a perinuclear distribution.

phenotypes.text: annular and polycyclic erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on trunk and proximal extremities

findings.statement: In the affected members of a family with annular epidermolytic ichthyosis, Joh et al. (1997) found a new 2-bp mutation in the KRT10 gene: a tandem CG-to-GA change on a single allele. This change replaces arginine with glutamate at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment. Based on this finding, the authors concluded that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis should be considered a variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.
quotes: Molecular analysis revealed a novel tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation in the same allele of keratin 10 in affected individuals, resulting in an arginine to glutamate substitution at residue 83 (R83E) of the 2B helical segment.
We conclude that annular epidermolytic ichthyosis should be considered a variant of bullous congenital ichthyosiform erythroderma.

variants.as_reported: tandem CG to GA 2-bp mutation, R83E

findings.statement: Joh et al. (1997) stated that the way annular epidermolytic ichthyosis is inherited fits an autosomal dominant pattern. The family they reported had affected members in two generations.
quotes: The pattern of inheritance of the disorder is consistent with an autosomal dominant mode of transmission.

relevance_reason: This is the original description of annular epidermolytic ichthyosis as a new phenotype in a single family.

findings.statement: Sahn et al. (1992) described a 30-year-old white woman whose bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions began at age 8 months. The blistering stopped at puberty, but the hyperkeratotic plaques remained. At age 27 years she developed many annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities. These plaques itched, grew slowly and then resolved.
quotes: A 30-year-old white woman developed bullous and ichthyosiform skin lesions at the age of 8 months. Blistering ceased at puberty, but the hyperkeratotic plaques persisted.
At the age of 27 years, she developed numerous annular and polycyclic, erythematous, hyperkeratotic plaques on the trunk and extremities that were pruritic, enlarged slowly, and then resolved.

phenotypes.text: annular and polycyclic erythematous hyperkeratotic plaques on trunk and extremities

findings.statement: Sahn et al. (1992) reported that the affected woman had five children, two of whom had a bullous type of ichthyosis. This is consistent with vertical transmission in the kindred.
quotes: She subsequently delivered five children, two of whom were affected with a bullous type of ichthyosis.

findings.statement: Sahn et al. (1992) found epidermolytic hyperkeratosis on histopathologic examination of the annular plaques. Electron microscopy showed interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings, which the authors considered consistent with either bullous ichthyotic erythroderma of Brocq or ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens. They suggested that the kindred might represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
quotes: Histopathologic examination of these annular plaques revealed epidermolytic hyperkeratosis.

Electron microscopic examination of the annular plaques showed interrupted perinuclear tonofilament rings consistent with either bullous ichthyotic erythroderma of Brocq or ichthyosis bullosa of Siemens.
This kindred may represent a new phenotype of epidermolytic (acanthokeratolytic) ichthyosis.
